rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Biogeochemical cycles move essential elements through living and non-living compartments. The carbon cycle (gaseous CO2) and the nitrogen cycle (N2 → NH3 → NO2- → NO3- → N2) are the most important; bacteria (Rhizobium, Nitrosomonas, Pseudomonas) drive key steps. The phosphorus cycle has no gaseous phase and is the slowest.…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text:
Carbon cycle: CO2 ↔ organic C (photosynthesis/respiration/decomposition); fossil fuel combustion → CO2
Nitrogen cycle: N2 → (fixation) NH3 → (nitrification) NO2- → NO3- → (assimilation) plants → (ammonification) NH3 → (denitrification) N2
Succession: primary (bare rock) / secondary (existing soil) → climax community

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: Nitrogen fixation converts N2 to ammonia (NH3/NH4+); nitrification converts ammonia to nitrite then nitrate; denitrification converts nitrate back to N2.  ·  Rhizobium (symbiotic, in legume root nodules) and Azotobacter (free-living, in soil) are both nitrogen-fixing bacteria.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: NEB expects detailed, labelled diagrams of the carbon and nitrogen cycles.  ·  The role of bacteria (Rhizobium, Nitrosomonas, Pseudomonas) in the nitrogen cycle is a very common exam point.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: Carbon cycle: forest (photosynthesis absorbs CO2) → animals (respiration releases CO2) → decomposers (release CO2) → atmosphere → ocean (dissolved CO2) → limestone (long-term storage).  ·  Nitrogen cycle: Rhizobium in pea root nodules fixes N2 → plants assimilate nitrate → animals eat plants → decomposers ammonify → denitrifying bacteria release N2.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: The carbon cycle has a gaseous phase (CO2); the phosphorus cycle does NOT have a gaseous phase.  ·  Primary succession starts on BARE ROCK (no soil); secondary succession starts on EXISTING SOIL (after disturbance).

rows.text: Nitrogen cycle: N2 → NH3 → NO2 → NO3 → plants → NH3 → N2.  ·  Rhizobium = fixation; Nitrosomonas = nitrification; Pseudomonas = denitrification.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Biogeochemical cycles: C, N, P, H, O move through biotic + abiotic compartments.  ·  Carbon cycle: gaseous (CO2); photosynthesis, respiration, decomposition, combustion.  ·  Nitrogen cycle: N2 → NH3 → NO2- → NO3- → assimilation → ammonification → N2.  ·  Bacteria: Rhizobium (fixation), Nitrosomonas (nitrification), Pseudomonas (denitrification).

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: Atmospheric nitrogen (N2) makes up ~78% of the air but is unusable by most organisms until fixed.  ·  Carbon dioxide is the main gaseous form of carbon in the carbon cycle.

rows.label: More practice
rows.text: Differentiate primary from secondary succession.  ·  What is a climax community? Give a Nepali example.  ·  Explain the role of bacteria in the nitrogen cycle (fixation, nitrification, denitrification).

rows.label: Extra solved
rows.text: Primary succession: bare rock after a volcanic eruption → lichens → mosses → grasses → shrubs → forest.  ·  Secondary succession: after a forest fire in Nepal → regrowth of grasses → shrubs → trees (faster than primary).

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: Biogeochemical cycles: the movement of elements (C, N, P, H, O) through biotic (living) and abiotic (non-living) compartments.  ·  Carbon cycle: atmospheric CO2 → photosynthesis (plants) → respiration (animals + plants) → decomposition → soil → oceans; combustion (fossil fuels) releases CO2; carbonate rocks (limestone) store carbon long-term.  ·  Nitrogen cycle: atmospheric N2 (78%) → nitrogen fixation (Rhizobium, Azotobacter, lightning) → ammonia (NH3) → nitrification (Nitrosomonas → nitrite; Nitrobacter → nitrate) → assimilation (plants) → ammonification (decomposers) → denitrification (Pseudomonas → N2).

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Gaseous vs non-gaseous cycles  ·  Phosphorus cycle: no gaseous phase; slowest cycle.  ·  Succession: primary (bare rock) vs secondary (existing soil); climax community is stable.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Climax: mature, stable community in equilibrium with the environment.  ·  Succession is a PREDICTABLE, directional process toward a stable climax community.  ·  Decomposition releases nutrients (C, N, P) back into the soil; without it, cycles would stop.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Climax community: a mature, stable oak-rhododendron forest on the Nepal hills.  ·  Primary vs secondary succession: key difference is the starting point (bare rock vs existing soil).  ·  Climax community: give a Nepali example (mature oak-rhododendron forest).

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Note that the phosphorus cycle has no gaseous phase.  ·  Memorise the steps of the carbon and nitrogen cycles.  ·  Learn the roles of Rhizobium, Nitrosomonas, and Pseudomonas.
